correctness.rationale: Equality in the Rayleigh bound forces the highest-frequency cycle mode to vanish wherever cos z is not -1. Even top mode has no zeros; each nonzero odd highest-frequency real mode has at most one zero, yielding the exhaustive parity-dependent singular locus and nullity one. At each singular point an odd analytic Lyapunov–Schmidt equation has scalar normal form -μt+c_n t³+O(μt³+t⁵), c_n=1/(6n) even and 1/(4n) odd, yielding two distinct nonzero inverse branches for μ>0. The exact argument works for all n≥3; embedded code checks n=3..15 but is not the proof.

evidence: Tree maps have independent edge coordinates; odd rings impose a phase-sum closure. General spectral invertibility sufficiency alone does not prove optimality.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Tree optimality does not imply odd-ring optimality: all-π is forbidden by odd-cycle closure. A new one-zero top-mode argument is needed for the odd ring; the tree paper does not imply the cubic inverse amplitude.

evidence: Known: diffeomorphic when h Λ<1; even case singular at antipodal state when h Λ=1; trees optimal. New: complete singular locus and odd-case threshold, plus three inverse branches and parity-dependent cubic coefficients.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The strict sufficient inequality is not logically equivalent to sharpness for odd closed rings. At the forbidden all-π odd configuration, the old even construction cannot be transplanted; the new kernel with a zero position and phase closure proves existence and uniqueness of the first odd singularities.

evidence: The ring paper proves a sufficient strict diffeomorphism interval and explicit sharpness for even rings; general tree sharpness treats unconstrained edge phases.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Neither source identifies the odd-cycle equality locus of the largest cycle-Laplacian Rayleigh quotient subject to closed edge phases. The cubic local inverse branch is a stronger, distinct statement than existence of a singular derivative.

value.rationale: Determines the first genuine failure of invertibility in an entire natural family of finite discrete phase-coupled oscillator rings, closing the odd-frustration gap in a bound previously sharp only for even cycles/trees. Exact number and location of incipient singularities (one versus n) and sharp parity-dependent inverse branch amplitude quantify loss of state reconstructibility under discretized coupling, not a routine parameter rescaling or tiny numerical improvement.
